title: Eco-evolutionary feedback reshapes competitive dynamics in an orchard fly system

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Dryad deposit doi:10.5061/dryad.wdbrv163s via the Dryad application programming interface (API): 19 files, 2,094,321 bytes total, CC0 licence, version 7 published 2026-07-11, and the exact file list with sizes (dev_time.csv 949 KB, temp_2024.csv 440 KB, starvation_tolerance.csv 182 KB, census_20251219.csv 169 KB, body_mass.csv 64 KB, fecundity.csv 35 KB, pupation.csv 28 KB, cage_nums.csv 2.8 KB, ordered_eff_sizes.csv 3.0 KB, plus 7 R/Rmd analysis scripts and README.md). I also confirmed via NCBI E-utilities that no GEO, SRA or BioProject record is linked to PubMed ID 42594213, so there is no sequencing component. Every attempt to retrieve file bytes failed: the API download endpoints return HTTP 401 ('must have current bearer token') and the public download paths return an Anubis/BotStopper proof-of-work challenge page, so I opened no rows, headers or units.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The experimental design (four pairs of Drosophilid fly species; monoculture, 'full evolution' mixture and 'limited evolution' mixture mesocosms; 5-10 generations; phenotypes = body mass, egg-to-adult development time, fecundity, pupation location, starvation tolerance; census of frequencies and abundances) comes from the Science abstract and the Dryad description. No row count for any file was verified; the inference that the number of mesocosm cages is in the tens rests on the design plus the 2,758-byte size of cage_nums.csv, not on an opened file.

a1_downloadable.note: Public CC0 Dryad deposit, no login or application needed for a human in a browser, but every programmatic route failed (API returns HTTP 401 without a bearer token; web download returns an Anubis bot-protection challenge). Files listed and sized, never opened.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Per the Dryad description each phenotype (body mass, development time, fecundity, pupation location, starvation tolerance) has its own CSV, so the outcome is a column, not something to construct. Not verified in the files.

a3_inputs_present.note: The only available predictors are experimental design factors (species, treatment, cage identity, generation, logged temperature); they are in the tables, but there are no molecular or sequence features of any kind.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are implied by phenotype (mass, days, egg counts, hours to death) and a README.md exists, but I could not read it, so this is unverified.

a5_enough_rows.note: Enough-rows failure in disguise, like the scCT-DB case: individual flies number in the thousands (dev_time.csv is 949 KB), but the independent unit for any question about competition-induced evolution is the mesocosm population, and the design (4 species pairs x 3 treatments x replicates, cage_nums.csv only 2,758 bytes) puts that in the tens, far under the ~400 needed even for classification. I could not open the files to count, which itself leaves the count unverifiable.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized; size is not the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Unverifiable: no file could be opened, so no count from the download can be compared with the paper or the Dryad record.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are direct laboratory and field measurements of fly phenotypes and cage censuses, not another model's output and not computed from the predictors.

backbone.name: none applicable
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop would suffice, but there is nothing to embed: no sequences, molecules, cells or images, only experimental treatment labels and phenotype measurements.

integration.join_key: species name only (free text), no standard identifier such as a taxonomy ID in the verified metadata
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could not write one: with no genomic, molecular or standard identifiers in the deposit, any join to a large resource would be decoration.

controls.positive_control: A working analysis should recover the textbook species-level differences in body mass and development time among the Drosophilid species, which the authors' own mixed models already show.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle treatment labels within species and confirm the competition-induced shift disappears.
controls.external_validation: The companion study by the same group (Leonard et al. 2026, Ecological Monographs, 'Seasonal evolution and its effects on competition') uses the same orchard mesocosm system, but it is the same lab and site, so it is not independent.

honest_claim_h3: A model here could only claim that an individual fly's phenotype differs by species, competition treatment and cage in one orchard mesocosm array over 5-10 generations in 2024 - which is exactly what the paper's mixed models already report.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use species identity, competition treatment and cage conditions to predict fly body size, development time and population abundance in mesocosms.
plain_idea.train_on: Individual-fly phenotype measurements and cage census counts from an outdoor mesocosm array of four Drosophilid species pairs; thousands of individual rows but only tens of independent cages, and no count was verified because the files could not be opened.
plain_idea.predict: A phenotype (body mass in mg, egg-to-adult development time in days, fecundity as egg counts, starvation survival time) or a species' abundance in a cage, each measured directly by the authors in the lab and by cage census.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Community ecologists testing whether competition-induced evolution stabilises coexistence would care about the biology, but the modelling adds nothing here: the predictors are experimental design factors that linear mixed models already handle optimally at this sample size.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict competition-relevant fly phenotypes or mesocosm abundance trajectories from species, competition treatment, cage and temperature. The feature space is a handful of experimental factor levels, the independent unit is the mesocosm (tens, not thousands), there are no sequences or molecules so no pretrained backbone applies, and the authors' linear mixed models are the statistically correct tool for exactly this design.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the 2 MB total deposit size listed by the Dryad API; nothing was timed because no file could be downloaded. Compute is irrelevant to the verdict - the constraint is the number of independent cages, not the hardware.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open cage_nums.csv and count the rows: if the number of mesocosm cages is in the tens, as its 2,758-byte size implies, every model-level question has an effective sample size of tens and the project is dead.

verdict_reason: Thousands of individual flies but only tens of independent mesocosms, which is the unit any competition question is asked at, so A5 fails in disguise; the files could not be opened at all because Dryad blocks programmatic download with a bot-protection challenge, so A7 is unverifiable too. Even granting the data, the only predictors are experimental treatment labels, no pretrained backbone fits, and the authors' mixed models are already the right tool.
